title: A protocol to measure lysosomal Zn2+ release through a genetically encoded Zn2+ indicator
protocol: Coat 18 mm Ø glass coverslips with a 10 mg/mL PDL solution overnight at 4°C.
Remove the PDL solution and wash the coverslips three times with PBS or sterilized water.
Store the coverslips in sterilized PBS or water at 4°C for future use within one week.
Seed cells in a 12-well plate containing pre-coated coverslips filled with 1 mL cell culture medium.
Check cell shape (adherent, fibroblast-like).
Check confluence of MeWo cells (60%–70%).
Transfect MeWo cells with 1 μg GZnP3-ML1 or 1 μg mCherry-ML1 and 1 μg GZnP3 using Lipofectamine 2000.
Add 100 μL Opti-MEM to each of two 1.5 mL tubes.
Add 4 μL Lipofectamine 2000 to one tube; incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Add 1 μg GZnP3-ML1 plasmid or 1 μg mCherry-ML1 and 1 μg GZnP3 to the other tube; incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Mix contents of both tubes gently and incubate at room temperature for 20 min.
Replace old culture medium with 300 μL fresh culture medium.
Gently drop DNA and Lipofectamine mixture onto cells.
Incubate cells in a 37°C 5% CO2 incubator for 4–6 h.
Discard all medium (∼ 500 μL) from the well.
Wash twice with 1 mL PBS.
Add 1 mL fresh warmed cell culture medium to the well.
Cells are ready for imaging 48 h post transfection.
Construct GZnP3, ML1 and GZnP3-ML1 on a pcDNA3.1 backbone with a CMV promoter.
Check the availability of GZnP3 within cells by imaging.
Acquire images using an EasyRatioPro imaging system (HORIBA).
Set up an inverted fluorescence microscope (Olympus IX71) equipped with a CoolSnap HQ2 camera and DeltaRam™ X monochromator.
Use a LPS220B power supply for the system.
Control the system automatically with EasyRatioPro software (version 1.12.121.86).
Set acquisition rate for continuous imaging or specified intervals as needed.
Acquire images using a 20× objective lens (Olympus).
Connect the outlet pipe with a liquid collection flask.
Attach a vacuum pump to the setup to collect waste solutions.
Prevent overflow within the perfusion chamber using the connected equipment.
Warm up the imaging buffer to 20°C–25°C.
Prepare ML-SA1 working solution at a concentration of 50 μM in Tyrode’s solution.
Load all solutions into the fluid reservoirs.
Place a coverslip with cells in the metal perfusion chamber.
Fill the perfusion chamber with Tyrode’s solution (∼0.2 mL).
Mount the perfusion chamber on an inverted microscope.
Ensure the coverslip is aligned and securely screwed to prevent liquid leakage.
Prepare the perfusion system, adjust inflow speed to 50–60 drops/min.
Adjust outflow speed to avoid overflow or drying of cells.
Turn on all power switches for the imaging setup.
Activate the DeltaRam-X monochromator.
Start the camera.
Turn on the computer and open EasyRatioPro software.
Turn off the room lights.
Ensure the experiment is performed in a dark environment to reduce background noise signals.
Clean the perfusion system with ethanol to avoid contamination from residual drugs.
Fill solution reservoirs (10 mL or 60 mL syringes) with solutions or ddH2O to prevent back-flow or air bubbles.
Allow solutions to flow through the entire perfusion system to ensure no air bubbles arise.
Activate ML1 using ML-SA1 to release Zn2+ from lysosomal lumen to cytosol.
Select GFP on the top menu in EasyRatioPro program.
Set up the channel for excitation at 488 nm in EasyRatioPro program.
In CHANNELS window, click the “R” and the “GFP” button.
In the IMAGE window, choose RAINBOW in PALETTE.
Adjust gain and exposure time to obtain low but visible basal fluorescent signals.
Set the read interval of each frame per 1–20 s, for MeWo cells, use 3 s interval.
Click the “RECORD” button in the TRANSPORT CONTROLS window.
Choose a ROI (Region of Interest) selector in the IMAGE window.
Circle out the cell to show the intensity curves in Graph window.
Record baseline for at least 3 min.
Add ML-SA1 (50 μM) to induce the lysosomal Zn2+ release.
Click PLAY button in the TRANSPORT CONTROL window.
Stain cells using FluoZin-3 AM and LysoTracker.
Challenge the stained cells with ML-SAs.
Obtain fluorescent images of the challenged cells.
Perform statistical analysis of the FluoZin-3 fluorescent intensity to show ML-SA-induced lysosomal signal decrease.
Use Glycyl-L-phenyalanine 2-naphthylamide (GPN) at a concentration of 200 μM for pre-treatment of cells.
Quantify fluorescence changes, normalizing to baseline fluorescence F0 as ΔF/F0.
Plot time on the x-axis and ΔF/F0 on the y-axis to observe changes in GZnP3 fluorescence over time.
Use ImageJ to analyze GZnP3 fluorescence.
Export the session data as an Excel file.
Average the F from time points before ML-SA1 application to get the baseline fluorescent intensity (F0) for the cell.
Calculate ΔF/F0 for individual time points using the equation provided.
Plot the time points on the x-axis and their corresponding ΔF/F0 on y-axis to reveal changes in GZnP3 signals over time.
Average ΔF/F0 from all recorded cells to generate an average time series of ΔF/F0.
In OriginPro, plot the time on the x-axis and the average ΔF/F0 on the y-axis to observe GZnP3 responses of all recorded cells over time.
Make a 1 M intermediate stock solution of ZnCl2 with ddH2O in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Add 5 μL of 1 M ZnCl2 to 50 mL imaging buffer to get 100 μM Zn2+ HBSS.
Store the long-term intermediate stock solution at 4°C for up to one month and short-term at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for up to one week.
Wash cells three times with 1 mL of Zn2+, Ca2+ free HBSS, 48 hours post-transfection.
Prepare the image chamber for imaging.
Mount the imaging chamber on an inverted microscope capable of exciting and recording GZnP3 fluorescence (488 nm excitation, 525 nm emission).
Acquire images using a CCD camera every 10–20 seconds.
Record baseline GZnP3 fluorescence for 3–5 minutes to ensure stability.
Add ML-SA1 to open lysosomal ML1 channel or add 100 μM TPEN to chelate Zn2+ from the GZnP3 indicator, bringing it to its minimum-fluorescent apo-state.
Incubate cells with TPEN for 5 minutes.
Wash cells three times with Zn2+, Ca2+ free HBSS after TPEN treatment.
Add 100 μM Zn²⁺ HBSS with 2.5 μM pyrithione to influx Zn²⁺.
Saturate the GZnP3 indicator to its fluorescent maximum.
Use ImageJ to analyze GZnP3 fluorescence.
